Please organize the results in one Markdown table with the following columns:
Date, the Concert’s English Name,  Host Country,  Host City, Host Venue

Don't ask me any questions, just output the results according to the columns without omitting cells arbitrarily. The output format is a markdown code block.

### Output Requirements
- **Format**: Markdown table wrapped in triple backticks with markdown specifier
- **Required Columns** (5): date, theconcert’senglishname, hostcountry, hostcity, hostvenue
- **Unique Key Columns**: date
- **Expected Rows**: 534 rows

**IMPORTANT**: Write the markdown table to `answer.txt` in the workspace.

**IMPORTANT**: You must NOT read the `ground_truth.csv` file in the workspace. Use web search to find all information.

**Note**: You may use available tools or skills in the system to complete this task.

and you need to complete the task in 480s.

2009 was Taylor Swift’s year, but someone forgot to tell the Fearless One that was it. She keeps going strong.

[Return to the current calendar](https://theswiftagency.com/calendar)

January

- January 19: Digital release of Today Was A Fairytale on iTunes.

- January 22: Hope for Haiti Telethon on all major networks at 8pm EST. Taylor will be performing live.

- January 27: Taylor will perform at  Unforgettable Evening event in LA, benefiting the EIF’s Women’s Cancer Research Fund.

- January 28: CBS re-runs the CSI episode with Taylor Swift. 9PM ET.

- January 29: She makes an appearance in the Early Show in CBS at 7AM ET.

- January 31: 52nd Grammy Awards in Los Angeles, California. It will be broadcasted on CBS, 8pm -11:30pm ET/PT. Taylor is nominated for 8 awards and scheduled to perform. She won 4: Best Country Song, Best Female Country Vocal, Best Country Album and Album of the Year 🙂

February

- February 4: The Fearless Tour 2010 begins with the Australian tour in Brisbane, Queensland.

- February 6: Australian tour concert in Sydney, New South Wales.

- February 7: Australian tour concert in Sydney, New South Wales.

- February 8: Australian tour concert in Newcastle, New South Wales.

- February 9: Release of the Valentine’s Day movie soundtrack in stores and online.

- February 10: Australian tour concert in Melbourne, Victoria.

- February 11: Australian tour concert in Melbourne, Victoria.

- February 12: Last concert of the Australian tour in Adelaide, Australia.

- February 12: Valentine’s Day movie opens.

- February 16: The 2010 Brit Awards in London, England.

- February 17: First ever Japan tour concert in Tokyo, Japan.

- February 26: [Caitlin Evanson](https://theswiftagency.wordpress.com/2009/11/15/caitlin-evanson/)‘s Birthday

March

- March 4: The US tour begins in Tampa, Florida.

- March 5: US tour concert in Orlando, Florida.

- March 7: US tour concert in Sunrise, Florida.

- March 10: US tour concert in Austin, Texas.

- March 11: US tour concert in Dallas, Texas.

- March 12: US tour concert in Corpus Christi, Texas.

- March 18: [Amos Heller](https://theswiftagency.wordpress.com/2009/11/18/amos-heller/)‘s Birthday.

- March 18: US tour concert in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

- March 19: US tour concert in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

- March 20: US tour concert in Charlottesville, Virginia.

- March 26: US tour concert in Detroit, Michigan.

- March 27: US tour concert in Detroit, Michigan.

- March 27: Kids Choice Awards on Nickelodeon. Taylor won for Favorite Song and Favorite Female Singer.

- March 28: US tour concert in Cincinnatti, Ohio.

- March 31: US tour concert in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.

April

- April 1: ACM voting period starts for Entertainer of the Year. Vote for Taylor at [VoteACM.com](http://www.voteacm.com/)

- April 1: US tour concert in Wichita, Kansas.

- April 1: [Mike Meadows](https://theswiftagency.wordpress.com/2009/11/18/mike-meadows/)‘ Birthday

- April 2: US tour concert in in Kansas City, Missouri.

- April 6: US tour concert in Denver, Colorado.

- April 7: US tour concert in Denver, Colorado.

- April 10: Tickets go on sale for the [CMT Awards](http://www.cmt.com/cmt-music-awards/) on June 9.

- April 10: US tour concert in Fresno, California.

- April 11: US tour concert in San Jose, California.

- April 15: US tour concert in Los Angeles, California.

- April 16: US tour concert in Los Angeles, California.

- April 18: [ACM Music Awards](http://www.acmcountry.com/). Live from Vegas at 8 p.m. ET/PT on CBS.http://www.voteacm.com

- April 18: [JUNO Awards](http://junoawards.ca/) 2010 in Toronto, Canada.

- April 19: Filming of [Brooks & Dunn: The Last Rodeo](http://www.brooks-dunn.com/) in Las Vegas, Nevada.

- April 29: US tour concert in Lexington, Kentucky.

- April 30: US tour concert in Columbia, South Carolina.

- April 30: [Grant Mickelson](https://theswiftagency.wordpress.com/2009/11/15/grant-mickelson/)‘s birthday.

May

- May 1: US tour concert in Raleigh, North Carolina.

- May 3: Costume Institute Benefit Event: “American Woman: Fashioning a National Identity”

- May 4: Time 100 Gala. Taylor will perform.

- May 6: US tour concert in Des Moines, Iowa.

- May 7: US tour concert in St Paul, Minnesota. Tickets go on sale for the new June 1st concert in Washington, D.C.

- May 8: US tour concert in Moline, Illinois.

- May 12: US tour concert in Newark, New Jersey.

- May 13: US tour concert in Newark, New Jersey. [Paul Sidoti](https://theswiftagency.wordpress.com/2009/11/18/paul-sidoti/)‘s Birthday. Taylor Swift evening auction via [MyWorkButterfly.com](http://www.myworkbutterfly.com/profiles/blogs/taylor-swift-celebrity-charity) starts to benefit VH1’s Save The Music.

- May 14: US tour concert in Uniondale, New York. Tickets go on sale for the Nashville Raising benefit concert for June 22.

- May 15: US tour concert in Uniondale, New York.

- May 18: 58th BMI Awards. Taylor Swift wins Song of the Year for Love Story and Most Performed Song along with Liz Rose for You Belong With Me.

- May 20: The Canadian tour starts in Ottawa, Ontario.

- May 21: Canadian tour concert in Toronto, Ontario. I captured it and I will remember it always.

- May 22: Canadian tour ends in Toronto, Ontario.

- May 23: CBS airs Brooks & Dunn: The Last Rodeo. Taylor’s auction at [MyWorkButterfly.com](http://www.myworkbutterfly.com/profiles/blogs/taylor-swift-celebrity-charity) ends.

- May 25: US tour concert in Houston, Texas. DVD being filmed?

- May 26: US tour concert in Houston, Texas.

- May 27: [Elizabeth Huett](https://theswiftagency.wordpress.com/2009/11/15/elizabeth-huett/)‘s Birthday.

- May 29: Bayou Country Superfest in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.

June

- June 1: US tour concert in Washington, Washington D.C.

- June 2: US tour concert in Washington, Washington D.C.

- June 5: Last official concert of the Fearless 2010 tour in Foxboro, Massachusetts.

- June 6: [MTV Movie Awards](http://www.mtv.com/ontv/movieawards/2010/best-kiss/). Taylor Squared considered for a Best Kiss nomination.

- June 9: [CMT Music Awards](http://www.cmt.com/cmt-music-awards/) at Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena. Live 8/7c

- June 13: Taylor Swift will be at the [CMA Music Fest 2010](http://www.cmafest.com/) in Nashville, Tennessee. She will be doing a Meet & Greet for 13 hours long that Sunday from 8AM to 9PM. Several fan activities will happen during the day, including an acoustic performance at 2pm. More details at [TaylorSwift.com](http://www.taylorswift.com/13-hour).

- June 17: Songwriters Hall of Fame. Taylor Swift receives the Hal David Starlight Award.

- June 19: Atlantis, Bahamas. She performs at the Imperial Ballroom.

- June 22: Nashville Raising: A Benefit Concert for Flood Recovery headed by Tim McGraw and Faith Hill. Taylor Swift is in the line-up.

July

- July 10: Taylor Swift performs at  the [Cavendish Beach Music Festival](http://www.cavendishbeachmusic.com/) in Cavendish, Prince Edward Island, Canada. Another Fearless Evening.

- July 20: Taylor Swift chats live with fans about her new album via [Ustream.tv](http://www.ustream.tv/user/TaylorSwift) at 4pm Central Daylight Time.

August

- August 4: After a leak, [Big Machine Records](http://www.bigmachinerecords.com/index.cfm?id=6&viewStory=411) jump starts the release of the first new single, Mine. Now available on [iTunes](http://itunes.apple.com/us/album/mine-single/id385990165)!

- August 7: Taylor Swift performs at the [Summer Sonic](http://www.summersonic.com/2010/tickets/) Festival in Osaka, Japan.

- August 8: Taylor Swift performs at the [Summer Sonic](http://www.summersonic.com/2010/tickets/) Festival in Tokio, Japan.

- August 9: [Teen Choice Awards](http://www.teenchoiceawards.com/index.php) in Los Angeles. Taylor Swift wins Choice Music Female Country Artist, Choice Country Album for Fearless, Choice Country song for Fifteen and Choice Movie Breakout Female for Valentine’s Day.

- August 16: The new single, Mine, from the third album, Speak Now is released on radio stations. Available now on [iTunes](http://www.bigmachinerecords.com/index.cfm?id=6&viewStory=411)!

- August 19: Pre-order Speak Now at [www.SpeakNow13.com](http://www.speaknow13.com).

- August 25: Voting closes for the VMAs!

- August 27: Mine will get its video premiere on CMT at 8pm ET/5PM PT. It will be a LIVE half-hour special event.

- August 31: The first batch of CMA nominations are announced at the Ryman Auditorium in Nashville, TN by Justin Moore and Chris Young.

September

- September 1: The remaining categories of the CMA nominations are announced by Miranda Lambert and Dierks Bentley on Good Morning America.

- September 1: [CMA Music Festival: Country’s Night To Rock](http://www.cmafest.com/) airs on ABC at 8/7c.

- September 9: Taylor Swift will perform at kickoff time in New Orleans for the Saints vs. Vikings game to be broadcast on NBC at 7:30pm ET.

- September 12: [MTV Video Music Awards](http://www.mtv.com/ontv/vma/2010/) airs on MTV at 9/8c. Taylor Swift was nominated for Female Video of the Year for Fifteen. Lady Gaga won it. Taylor performs Innocent for the first time ever, a song dedicated to the previous VMA incident and forgiveness.

- September 18: Tickets go on sale for the [44th CMA Awards](http://www.cmaawards.com/), which takes place November 10.

- September 21: Voting period ends for [J-14 Teen Icon Awards](http://www.j-14.com/2010/09/introducing-j-14s-teen-icon-awards-official-nominations.html).

- September 22: Voting period ends for the [Country Weekly](http://www.countryweekly.com/sexiest_2010/vote/surveys/723) most beautiful woman in country music.

- September 23: Taylor Swift performs at the [All For The Hall fundraiser at Club Nokia](http://www.clubnokia.com/eventdetail.php?id=28714), Los Angeles that benefits the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum.

- September 27: Taylor Swift visits Milan, Italy.

- September 28: She is scheduled to perform on X-Factor Italy.

- September 29: She attends Roberto Cavalli’s 40th Anniversary gala dinner and party at Ecole Superiure des Beaux Arts in Paris, France.

- September 30: Taylor Swift is scheduled for an interview at [NRJ](http://www.nrj.fr/music-509/exclus-nrj-526/article/249731-taylor-swift-en-interview-dans-le-6-9-gagne-tes-places-.html) in Paris, France. You can [enter the contest](http://www.nrj.fr/music-509/exclus-nrj-526/article/249731-taylor-swift-en-interview-dans-le-6-9-gagne-tes-places-.html) to be part of the audience.

October

- October 1: CMT’s [Speak Now with Taylor Swift in New York City](http://winwithtaylor.com/) contest registration closes.

- October 4:Speak Now will get a 30-second preview on Comcast On Demand and [XfinityTv.com](http://www.xfinitytv.com/) starting one minute past midnight. E! News will show a clip and interview in the evening.

- October 5:Speak Now goes on sale on iTunes.

- October 9: Taylor Swift performs at the [Grand Ole Opry](http://search2.opry.com/?view=events&q=Taylor)! Dolly Parton performs on the very same night! [Get your tickets now](http://search2.opry.com/?view=events&q=Taylor).

- October 11:Back To December will get a 30-second preview on Comcast On Demand and [XfinityTv.com](http://www.xfinitytv.com/) starting one minute past midnight. E! News will show a clip and interview in the evening.

- October 12:Back To December goes on sale on iTunes. The Glamour magazine with Taylor Swift’s interview, photoshoot and cover comes out in newsstands.

- October 18:Mean will get a 30-second preview on Comcast On Demand and [XfinityTv.com](http://www.xfinitytv.com/) starting one minute past midnight. E! News will show a clip and interview in the evening.

- October 18: Taylor Swift performs in a private concert at a secret location in Paris! Promoted by [Goom Radio](http://www.goomradio.fr/#page=radio/just-hits/2010/10/07/taylor-swift-en-showcase--gagne-tes-invits).

- October 18: Royal Caribbean International launches its contest [The Allure of Taylor Swift](http://theallureoftaylor.com/#). You win a 7-night cruise for two on the Bahamas including two tickets for Taylor’s on board concert. The promotion period starts now and runs until October 29. The cruise dates are tentatively scheduled for January 16-23, 2011. Sorry, only US residents eligible.

- October 19:Mean goes on sale on iTunes.

- October 22: The ticket sales for the UK concerts on March 22, 29 and 30 of 2011 open on [SeeTickets](http://www2.seetickets.com/see/event.asp?artist=TAYLOR+SWIFT). [Play.com](http://www.play.com/Music/CD/4-/15957600/Speak-Now/Product.html) will give you a ticket pre-sales code if you pre-order the [Speak Now CD](http://www.play.com/Music/CD/4-/15957600/Speak-Now/Product.html) or [Speak Now Deluxe Edition CD](http://www.play.com/Music/CD/4-/16686744/Speak-Now/Product.html)! More at [Play.com](http://www.play.com/Music/CD/4-/15957600/Speak-Now/Product.html).

- October 22: Taylor Swift appears on [Paul O’Grady Live](http://www.itv.com/paulogrady) in London, England.

- October 22, 23 and 24: Taylor Swift’s Journey To Fearless premieres on [The Hub](http://www.hubworld.com/) network.

- October 22: Story Of Us will get a 30-second preview on Comcast On Demand and [XfinityTv.com](http://www.xfinitytv.com/) starting one minute past midnight. E! News will show the clip in the evening.

- October 23: Last chance to send your video entries for the [Team Hug](http://www.teamhug.org/)contest! Closes at 5pm Eastern time.

- October 25: Speak Now WORLDWIDE DATE RELEASE on iTunes and on major music retailers around the world.

- October 25: Tickets go on sale for a lot of tour concert dates! See February and March for ticket links.

- October 25: [103.7 KISS-FM](http://www.1037kissfm.com/) in Milwaukee will be [taken over](http://wxss.taylorswifttakeover.com/) by Taylor Swift at noon.

- October 25: A group of winners of contests held around the world will join Taylor for a private performance at the United Nations in New York City. [Taylor Swift Live Stream from New York City](http://www.cmt.com/shows/events/taylor_swift_live_stream/) will be available on many of MTV Networks’ web properties, including CMT.com, MTV.com, VH1.com and websites across Europe, Asia, Australia and Latin America at 7PM Eastern, 6PM Central. Now also available on [Ustream](http://www.ustream.tv/taylorswift).

- October 25: Taylor Swift takes over [Dial-Global Hot Country Forum](http://www.dial-global.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=244:taylor-swift-takes-over-dial-globals-hot-country-format&catid=1:on-the-dial-press&Itemid=92) from 8pm to 9pm EST.

- October 26: Taylor will perform live for fans from Rockefeller Plaza on the [Today Show](http://today.msnbc.msn.com/) as part of their fall concert series. Fans can apply for passes to the show at: [http://today.msnbc.msn.com/id/30012397](http://today.msnbc.msn.com/id/30012397) . That night, she will do an interview and performance on the [Late Show with David Letterman](http://www.cbs.com/late_night/late_show/). The [Today Show](http://today.msnbc.msn.com/) airs on NBC from 7:00 – 11:00 a.m. (all time zones), and [Late Show with David Letterman](http://www.cbs.com/late_night/late_show/) airs on CBS at 11:30 p.m. (ET/PT).

- October 27: Taylor’s day starts with [Live! With Regis & Kelly](http://regisandkelly.go.com/) where she will do an interview and performance. The show airs on ABC affiliates nationwide, check for listings by area. That afternoon, she will visit Scholastic’s New York headquarters, where she will take time out from her busy release week schedule for a special literacy event, [Read Now! with Taylor Swift](http://www.scholastic.com/readeveryday/readnow.htm), as part of the company’s 90th Anniversary Literacy campaign ([register here](http://vxlive.feedroom.com/feedroom/http/4000/5172/5174/7045/Lobby/default.htm)). Later in the day, she will visit Madame Tussaud’s New York – the famed Times Square wax attraction — for the unveiling of her original wax figure.

- October 27: Taylor will now be appearing at the JetBlue terminal, Gate 14 (there is no Gate 13, superstitious much?) at Kennedy International Airport in New York City on Wednesday, October 27. Taylor Swift has a chartered flight from New York to Los Angeles with very lucky fans included and even an improvised concert during the flight.

- October 28:[Ellen DeGeneres Show](http://ellen.warnerbros.com/) will celebrate the release of Speak Now by once again devoting an entire hour-long show to throwing Taylor’s official album release party. Participate in Ellen’s [Ultimate Taylor Swift Fan](http://ellen.warnerbros.com/show/respond/?PlugID=463#ixzz12O0vM7jI) contest!

- October 29: Taylor Swift performs at Hollywood and Highland in Los Angeles, California.

- October 29: The Royal Caribbean International contest [The Allure of Taylor Swift](http://theallureoftaylor.com/#) entry period closes. The cruise dates are tentatively scheduled for January 16-23, 2011. Sorry, only US residents eligible.

November

- November 1: The Speak Now Album Release Party will air on the [Ellen DeGeneres Show](http://ellen.warnerbros.com/) on Monday, November 1st (syndicated, check local listings).

- November 2: Taylor will perform on [Dancing With the Stars](http://abc.go.com/shows/dancing-with-the-stars), airing on ABC at 9:00 p.m. (ET/PT).

- November 4: Taylor gets interviewed on CTV’s Canada AM. Enter 99.9FM’s [contest to be in the audience](http://toronto.virginradio.ca/Channels/listentowin/Story.aspx?ID=1303207)!

- November 4: Taylor Swift will be at the [MuchMusic](http://blog.muchmusic.com/taylor-swift-is-coming-to-muchmusic/) building in Toronto, Canada at 5pm Eastern time.

- November 9: The [BMI Awards](http://www.bmi.com/press/entry/548690).

- November 10: The 44th Annual [CMA Awards](http://www.cmaawards.com/) ceremony takes place live from the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville, TN. The event airs on ABC at 8/7c. Taylor Swift is nominated for Female Vocalist of the Year. She also is scheduled to perform. Update: She lost to Miranda Lambert.

- November 11: The CMA Country Christmas is taped. Taylor is not scheduled to appear but it’s still a major Country Music show.

- November 14: Taylor is scheduled to perform at the [BBC Radio 1’s Teen Awards](http://www.bbc.co.uk/radio1/teenawards/2010/about/).

- November 16: Speak Now is released on vinyl.

- November 17: TV appearance on [Fuji TV/SmapXSmap Japan TV](http://www.fujitv.co.jp/en/).

- November 18: TV appearance on [Nippon TV/Zoom In Japan TV](http://www.ntv.co.jp/english/).

- November 21: The [American Music Awards](http://abc.go.com/shows/american-music-awards) are broadcast live on ABC at 8pm Eastern time. The winners will be decided via online voting through [ABC.com](http://www.ama.abc.com/) and [AMAvote.com](http://www.amavote.com/). Taylor Swift is nominated for Favorite Female Country Artist. Update! Voting is now closed.

- November 22: Taylor Swift will appear on the Tonight Show with Jay Leno. Check your local TV listings.

- November 24: Taylor Swift’s performance of Back To December will air on The Ellen Degeneres Show. Check your local TV listings.

- November 24: Taylor Swift will appear on the Chelsea Lately show. Check your local TV listings.

- November 25: “Taylor Swift – Speak Now” will document the days of the Speak Now album release including a trip from New York City to Los Angeles, her multiple performances, behind the scenes footage and her concert 30,000 feet in the air on a plane ride across the country. The special airs on [NBC](http://www.nbc.com/) at 8PM Eastern Time.

December

- December 1: [E! Entertainment Special](http://www.eonline.com) on Taylor Swift at 10pm Eastern time.

- December 3: Atlanta, Los Angeles, San Jose, Sacramento and Toronto are on sale to the general public on [Ticketmaster](http://www.ticketmaster.com/search?q=taylor+swift) at 10:00am.

- December 3: The first ever [CMT Artists of the Year](http://www.cmt.com/shows/events/artists-of-the-year/index.jhtml) airing Dec. 3 at 8/7c on CMT. Taylor Swift is among the honored ones.

- December 4: Foxborough is on sale to the general public on [Ticketmaster](http://www.ticketmaster.com/search?q=taylor+swift) at 10:00am. Montreal is on sale at [Evenko](http://www.evenko.ca/en/show/event/taylor-swift-4842).

- December 4: The voting for the [American Country Awards](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php) closes. You can vote at [theacas.com](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php). Taylor is up for Artist of the Year: Female and Touring Artist of the Year. [Vote vote vote](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php)!

- December 6: The first ever [American Country Awards](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php) show will air on the Fox Network. Taylor is up for Artist of the Year, Female Artist of the Year and Touring Artist of the Year. You can vote at [theacas.com](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php). Taylor is up for Artist of the Year: Female and Touring Artist of the Year. [Vote vote vote](http://theacas.com/vote-artistawards.php)!

- December 10: The concert dates of August 27 and 28 in Los Angeles, CA at the Staples Center are on sale to the general public on [Ticketmaster](http://www.ticketmaster.com/search?q=taylor+swift) at 10:00am.

- December 12: The Hub will rerun their Taylor Swift special Journey To Fearless.

- December 13: Taylor Swift turns 21 years old 🙂

[Return to the current calendar](https://theswiftagency.com/calendar)

(Sources: [TaylorSwift.com](http://www.taylorswift.com), and way too many to enumerate!)

Taylor Swift, the Grammy-winning artist with a career spanning over two decades, needs no introduction. Her music has resonated with millions across the globe, and the Eras Tour is a testament to that enduring connection.

Unlike previous tours focused on a single album release, ‘Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour’ is a monumental event taking fans on a journey through her incredible career. From the country twang of her debut to the pop perfection of “1989” and the alternative explorations of “folklore” and “evermore,” every era will have its moment to shine.

Are you ready to revisit your favorite albums and sing along to iconic hits? This comprehensive guide provides everything you need to know about the Taylor Swift Eras Tour in 2024, including confirmed dates, locations, and even some [travel tips](https://blog.tours4fun.com/)!

Image by Paolo V

## Confirmed Taylor Swift Eras Tour Dates & Locations

The Eras Tour commenced on March 17, 2023, in Glendale, [Arizona](https://www.tours4fun.com/sp/d-arizona/), United States. As of now, there are about 60 concerts remaining in 2024.

Currently, Taylor is gearing up for the European leg, with confirmed shows across major cities like Paris, [London](http://tours4fun.com/sp/d-london/), and Stockholm. Canada dates will follow in November and December, with stops in [Vancouver](https://www.tours4fun.com/sp/d-vancouver/) and Toronto (which is also the final show of the Eras Tour).

Here are the confirmed dates and locations for the upcoming Taylor Swift Eras Tour 2024:

Europe (May – August 2024)

Paris, France – Paris La Défense Arena (May 9-12)

Stockholm, Sweden – Friends Arena (May 17-19)

Hamburg, Germany – Volksparkstadion (July 23-24)

Munich, Germany – Olympiastadion (July 27-28)

Vienna, Austria – Ernst-Happel-Stadion (August 8-10)

Canada (November – December 2024)

Vancouver, British Columbia – BC Place (December 6-8)

The tour schedule is collated on March 20, 2024, please visit the [official website](https://www.taylorswift.com/tour/) for the most up-to-date information.

Image by Ronald Woan

## What to Expect at the Taylor Swift Eras Tour 2024

The Eras Tour will be a visual and musical feast that will take fans on a chronological journey through Taylor’s classic musical era. From her debut album to her latest chart-topping hits, fan favorites will be featured.

While specifics are yet to be revealed, here’s what we can anticipate based on Taylor Swift’s past tours and the “Eras” theme:

Multiple eras, Multiple hits: The core concept of the tour – showcasing her music from different eras of her career – is a clear crowd-pleaser. Fans get to relive their favorite eras with elaborate stage designs and costume changes.

Deep cuts and fan favorites: Swift is reportedly mixing in fan-requested songs alongside the hits, making the setlist unpredictable and exciting for longtime fans.

Relatable moments: The recent release of the “Errors Tour” content within the “Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour Movie (Taylor’s Version)” shows her willingness to embrace imperfections. This adds a layer of relatability and humor to the live experience.

Surprise guests and throwbacks: There have been reports of surprise guest appearances and deep cuts from her discography that even the most hardcore Swifties might not expect.

## How to Get Tickets for the Taylor Swift Eras Tour

Tickets for the Eras Tour are already selling out fast! Here’s how to secure your spot for the upcoming shows:

Official website: Check Taylor Swift’s official website (https://www.taylorswift.com/tour/) for ticket links and on-sale dates for upcoming shows.

Ticketmaster: Ticketmaster is the official ticketing partner for most of the tour dates. Visit their website (https://www.ticketmaster.com/) and search for “Taylor Swift Eras Tour” to see available tickets.

Secondary marketplaces: Platforms like StubHub and SeatGeek may offer resale tickets, although prices can be significantly higher than face value..

Taylor Swift, the Grammy-winning artist with a career spanning over two decades, needs no introduction. Her music has resonated with millions across the globe, and the Eras Tour is a testament to that enduring connection.

Unlike previous tours focused on a single album release, ‘Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour’ is a monumental event taking fans on a journey through her incredible career. From the country twang of her debut to the pop perfection of “1989” and the alternative explorations of “folklore” and “evermore,” every era will have its moment to shine.

Are you ready to revisit your favorite albums and sing along to iconic hits? This comprehensive guide provides everything you need to know about the Taylor Swift Eras Tour in 2024, including confirmed dates, locations, and even some [travel tips](https://blog.tours4fun.com/)!

Image by Paolo V

## Confirmed Taylor Swift Eras Tour Dates & Locations

The Eras Tour commenced on March 17, 2023, in Glendale, [Arizona](https://www.tours4fun.com/sp/d-arizona/), United States. As of now, there are about 60 concerts remaining in 2024.

Currently, Taylor is gearing up for the European leg, with confirmed shows across major cities like Paris, [London](http://tours4fun.com/sp/d-london/), and Stockholm. Canada dates will follow in November and December, with stops in [Vancouver](https://www.tours4fun.com/sp/d-vancouver/) and Toronto (which is also the final show of the Eras Tour).

Here are the confirmed dates and locations for the upcoming Taylor Swift Eras Tour 2024:

## What to Expect at the Taylor Swift Eras Tour 2024

The Eras Tour will be a visual and musical feast that will take fans on a chronological journey through Taylor’s classic musical era. From her debut album to her latest chart-topping hits, fan favorites will be featured.

Multiple eras, Multiple hits: The core concept of the tour – showcasing her music from different eras of her career – is a clear crowd-pleaser. Fans get to relive their favorite eras with elaborate stage designs and costume changes.

Deep cuts and fan favorites: Swift is reportedly mixing in fan-requested songs alongside the hits, making the setlist unpredictable and exciting for longtime fans.

Relatable moments: The recent release of the “Errors Tour” content within the “Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour Movie (Taylor’s Version)” shows her willingness to embrace imperfections. This adds a layer of relatability and humor to the live experience.

Surprise guests and throwbacks: There have been reports of surprise guest appearances and deep cuts from her discography that even the most hardcore Swifties might not expect.

[Taylor Swift](//theboot.com/tag/TaylorSwift/) has announced more dates for her Speak Now World tour 2011, which kicks off February 9 in Singapore, as we [reported](//theboot.com/2010/10/27/taylor-swift-world-tour-2011/) last month. Next year's trek is currently scheduled to play 87 shows in 19 countries spanning four continents and will include six stadium shows -- Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass., Detroit's Ford Field, Pittsburgh's Heinz Field, Philadelphia's Lincoln Financial Field, Kansas City's Arrowhead Stadium and Dallas Cowboys Stadium.
During the first few months of 2011, Taylor will play shows overseas in Asia and Europe, before kicking off her North American tour in Omaha, Neb., on May 27. Tour dates in Australia and New Zealand will be announced at a later date.
"I'm so excited to go back out on tour again in 2011!" says Taylor. "The Fearless Tour was so much fun and even more unforgettable than I ever imagined, and I can't wait to get back out and play my new music from '[Speak Now](http://www.amazon.com/Speak-Now-Taylor-Swift/dp/B003WTE886/ref=sr_1_1?s=music&ie=UTF8&qid=1290548190&sr=1-1)!' The fans have been so amazing, and I'm thrilled to play in new cities around the world and meet even more of my fans in 2011!"
Taylor's 15-month, 107-date Fearless 2009 / 2010 tour sold out arenas and stadiums in 88 cities in five countries and grossed nearly $64 million.
"With me going on my first headlining tour last year, there's a reason why it lasted 15 months, instead of the half a year it was going to last," the 20-year-old superstar explains. "I just could not stop touring. I could not put the Fearless tour down. I loved it so much, because when I'm on that stage and I'm performing on my concert tour, I'm going through all the emotions that I went through when I wrote the songs, in front of all these people, and I feel like we're all in it together. It's unbelievable the feeling that I get when I'm standing there knowing that they know what I mean."
If you can't wait until her tour kicks off next year, catch Taylor performing several songs from her new album, 'Speak Now,' on Thanksgiving (November 25) night. Her one-hour '[Taylor Swift: Speak Now](//theboot.com/2010/11/19/taylor-swift-nbc-tv-special/)' television special, which takes fans on a whirlwind trip from New York to Los Angeles, airs at 8:00 PM ET on NBC.

Taylor Swift officially announced on her Facebook Page today a 2010 leg of her Fearless Tour!

Taylor Swift, who this weekend will play the final four shows of her groundbreaking, sold-out FEARLESS 2009 Tour, announced today that she will bring the FEARLESS Tour back to the fans in 2010. Tickets for the Taylor Swift FEARLESS 2010 tour will go on sale later this month, with ticket prices starting at $25.
Taylor, who at 19 is the youngest artist in history to be nominated for the Country Music Association’s prestigious Entertainer of the Year Award, will kick off her FEARLESS 2010 Tour on February 4th in Brisbane, Australia and play five shows Down Under before beginning her North American run on March 4th in Tampa, Florida. In 2010, Taylor will headline 37 shows in 29 cities in 22 states and provinces in the US and Canada.
“I’m so excited to take the Fearless tour back out on the road again in 2010!” says Taylor. “This year’s tour has been so much fun and even more unforgettable than I ever imagined. The fans have been so amazing, and I’m thrilled to play in new cities and see even more of my fans on the 2010 FEARLESS Tour!”
The Taylor Swift FEARLESS 2009 TOUR was the hottest ticket of the year, wowing fans and critics worldwide. Capacity crowds packed arenas around the globe -- every show on the tour sold out within minutes, including one at Madison Square Garden in one minute, and one at Los Angeles’ STAPLES center in just two minutes. The blockbuster tour was chronicled in the one-hour primetime NBC network special Dateline: On Tour With Taylor Swift.
Here’s what some of the nation’s top critics had to say about Taylor Swift and the FEARLESS 2009 Tour:
“Swift’s fans don’t just believe in her savvy songwriting and gracious, magnetic stage presence. They trust her as a peer. And if the unerring pleasures of her set – and the crowd’s Beatles-sized reactions – were any indication, they’ll be trusting her for a long time.” – The Los Angeles Times
“Country queen Taylor Swift charms the L.A. crowd.” – The Hollywood Reporter

Is [Taylor Swift](//theboot.com/tags/taylor-swift/) coming to a city near you? She has revealed the tour dates for her 1989 World Tour, and so far, there are a lot of them, spanning six months and going across the country ... and beyond.
The singer made the announcement on ABC's 'Good Morning America' and also shared a YouTube video with fans. She expressed her excitement about the tour, saying, "So yeah, #The1989WorldTour is happening!! Go to [TaylorSwift.com](http://taylorswift.com) for details. I CANNOT WAIT!"
The 1989 World Tour is set (so far) to play in five countries, and the venues include both arenas and stadiums. It kicks off May 20, 2015, in Bossier City, La., at the CenturyLink Center and ends on Halloween 2015 in Tampa, Fla.
Australian singer-songwriter Vance Joy will open the North American dates, while Shawn Mendes will join the stadium shows. Swift recently [covered](//tasteofcountry.com/taylor-swift-riptide-vance-joy-video/) Joy's 'Riptide' for a BBC radio show -- and now it makes perfect sense why she chose that song.
Australian and Asian concert dates will be revealed later on. The first tickets will go on sale to the general public Nov. 14, but TaylorSwift.com members and American Express card members will have access beginning Nov. 7.

Is [Taylor Swift](//theboot.com/tags/taylor-swift/) coming to a city near you? She has revealed the tour dates for her 1989 World Tour, and so far, there are a lot of them, spanning six months and going across the country ... and beyond.
The singer made the announcement on ABC's 'Good Morning America' and also shared a YouTube video with fans. She expressed her excitement about the tour, saying, "So yeah, #The1989WorldTour is happening!! Go to [TaylorSwift.com](http://taylorswift.com) for details. I CANNOT WAIT!"
The 1989 World Tour is set (so far) to play in five countries, and the venues include both arenas and stadiums. It kicks off May 20, 2015, in Bossier City, La., at the CenturyLink Center and ends on Halloween 2015 in Tampa, Fla.
Australian singer-songwriter Vance Joy will open the North American dates, while Shawn Mendes will join the stadium shows. Swift recently [covered](//tasteofcountry.com/taylor-swift-riptide-vance-joy-video/) Joy's 'Riptide' for a BBC radio show -- and now it makes perfect sense why she chose that song.
Australian and Asian concert dates will be revealed later on. The first tickets will go on sale to the general public Nov. 14, but TaylorSwift.com members and American Express card members will have access beginning Nov. 7.

- Published: Oct. 27, 2012, 11:35 a.m.

By

- [John Gonzalez | gonzo@mlive.com](https://www.mlive.com/staff/jgonzale/)

Taylor Swift will headline 58 shows in 45 cities in 29 states and 3 provinces in 2013 on her "Red" tour. She performs May 4 at Ford Field.
taylorswift.com

[Taylor Swift](http://topics.mlive.com/tag/Taylor%20Swift/index.html) announced dates for her 2013 "Red" tour, including several stadium dates.
One of those stadium dates is May 4 at Ford Field in Detroit. Tickets will go on sale at 10 a.m. Nov. 16.
The others: Heinz Field in Pittsburgh, Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Cowboys Stadium in Dallas, Gillette Stadium near Boston and Soldier Field in Chicago.
Overall, Swifty is scheduled to headline 58 shows in 45 cities in 29 states and 3 provinces in 2013. It will kick off March 13 in Omaha, Nebraska and continue through September.
Every show will include tickets priced at under $50. The first tickets will go on sale on Nov. 16, and on-sale information is available now at [TaylorSwift](http://www.TaylorSwift.com).com.
On her website, Swift said she is thrilled about bringing the show to her fans.
"I didn't think I could be any more excited about my Red album, but then I start thinking about how I'm going to put the new show together for The Red Tour," she said.
"I have so many ideas about how to really bring this music to life, and I can't wait to share the new show with all my fans!"
Swift also announced that British singer-songwriter Ed Sheeran will be her special guest. They worked together on the duet "Everything Has Changed" off "Red."

The Reputation Stadium Tour was the fifth headlining [concert tour](/page/Concert_tour) by American [singer-songwriter](/page/Singer-songwriter) [Taylor Swift](/page/Taylor_Swift), and her first to exclusively play stadium venues, launched to promote her sixth studio album, [Reputation](/page/Reputation) (2017).[[1]](#ref-1)[[2]](#ref-2)
The tour consisted of 53 shows across seven countries—[United States](/page/United_States), [Canada](/page/Canada), [United Kingdom](/page/United_Kingdom), [Ireland](/page/Ireland), [Australia](/page/Australia), [New Zealand](/page/New_Zealand), and [Japan](/page/Japan)—beginning on May 8, 2018, at [University of Phoenix](/page/University_of_Phoenix) Stadium in [Glendale, Arizona](/page/Glendale,_Arizona), and ending on November 21, 2018, at [Tokyo Dome](/page/Tokyo_Dome) in [Tokyo](/page/Tokyo), [Japan](/page/Japan).[[3]](#ref-3)[[4]](#ref-4) Featuring elaborate production elements including a snake-inspired stage design, massive LED screens, hydraulic platforms, and fireworks, the shows typically lasted nearly two hours and included a mix of [Reputation](/page/Reputation) tracks alongside hits from Swift's earlier albums, with nightly acoustic "surprise songs" performed on secondary stages.[[1]](#ref-1)[[2]](#ref-2)[[5]](#ref-5)
Opening acts varied by leg, with [Camila Cabello](/page/Camila_Cabello) and [Charli XCX](/page/Charli_XCX) supporting the North American and European dates, while [Broods](/page/Broods) joined for the [Oceania](/page/Oceania) shows.[[6]](#ref-6) The tour was a commercial juggernaut, grossing $345.7 million from 2.9 million tickets sold, marking it as the highest-grossing U.S. tour in boxscore history at the time and Swift's biggest earner until her [Eras Tour](/page/The_Eras_Tour).[[7]](#ref-7)[[8]](#ref-8)[[9]](#ref-9)
Critics praised the tour for its high-energy spectacle, Swift's vocal prowess, and thematic cohesion tying into Reputation's narrative of resilience and reinvention, with reviews hailing it as the peak of her live performances and one of the best tours of 2018.[[10]](#ref-10)[[1]](#ref-1) Notable moments included surprise guest appearances by artists like [Maren Morris](/page/Maren_Morris), [Tim McGraw](/page/Tim_McGraw), and [Faith Hill](/page/Faith_Hill), as well as Swift's philanthropic efforts, including inviting 2,000 foster and adopted children to a pre-tour rehearsal concert in [Arizona](/page/Arizona) for free.[[11]](#ref-11)[[12]](#ref-12)[[13]](#ref-13)
The tour's Dallas show on October 6, 2018, was documented in the Netflix concert film Taylor Swift: Reputation Stadium Tour, directed by Paul Dugdale, which premiered on December 31, 2018, and highlighted behind-the-scenes preparations alongside full performances, earning acclaim for its intimate portrayal of Swift's artistry amid intense media scrutiny. The film was later made available for purchase and rental on various platforms after leaving Netflix in 2023.[[14]](#ref-14)[[15]](#ref-15)[[16]](#ref-16)

## Background and development

### Announcement and promotion

Taylor Swift announced the Reputation Stadium Tour on November 13, 2017, via her official website and social media channels, shortly after the release of her sixth studio album, Reputation, on November 10, 2017.[[17]](#ref-17) The initial reveal detailed the first leg of 27 stadium shows across North America, set to commence on May 8, 2018, at University of Phoenix Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, and conclude on October 6, 2018, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.[[18]](#ref-18) This tour marked Swift's first all-stadium production and was explicitly positioned in support of Reputation, an album exploring themes of intense media scrutiny on her personal life and personal empowerment amid public backlash.[[19]](#ref-19)
Promotional efforts for the tour were deeply integrated with the album's marketing campaign, which had begun earlier in 2017 with a deliberate [social media](/page/Social_media) blackout across Swift's platforms in late August, followed by cryptic teasers such as timestamped videos and newspaper-style advertisements hinting at reclaiming her [narrative](/page/Narrative).[[20]](#ref-20) Key singles like "...Ready for It?", released as a promotional track on September 3, 2017, and sent to radio on October 24, 2017, built anticipation by showcasing the album's bold, trap-influenced sound that aligned with the tour's high-energy [stadium](/page/Stadium) format.[[21]](#ref-21) Exclusive merchandise lines, including apparel and accessories themed around Reputation's snake motif and dark aesthetic, were launched alongside the [album](/page/Album) and extended into tour-specific items available through presales, further immersing fans in the album's [narrative](/page/Narrative) of resilience.[[22]](#ref-22)
To facilitate fan access, Swift implemented the Taylor Swift Tix program, a verified fan system where participants earned "boosts" toward presale eligibility by engaging with her [music](/page/Music), such as purchasing [Reputation](/page/Reputation) or streaming videos, rewarding dedicated supporters with priority entry starting December 5, 2017.[[23]](#ref-23) General ticket sales opened on December 13, 2017, via [Ticketmaster](/page/Ticketmaster), with subsequent announcements adding European dates in December 2017, [Oceania](/page/Oceania) leg in May 2018, and Japan dates in August 2018, the tour ultimately expanding to 53 shows across [North America](/page/North_America), [Europe](/page/Europe), [Oceania](/page/Oceania), and [Asia](/page/Asia) to meet demand, emphasizing Swift's strategy of direct fan engagement over traditional media promotion.[[24]](#ref-24)[[25]](#ref-25)

### Production and staging

The production of Taylor Swift's Reputation Stadium Tour was led by show director and lighting designer Baz Halpin, who oversaw the integration of theatrical elements with high-tech visuals to embody the album's themes of media scrutiny and rebirth.[[26]](#ref-26) Associate director Melissa Garcia collaborated closely with Halpin to choreograph transitions between performance segments, while [production designer](/page/Production_designer) Tamlyn Wright crafted the overall aesthetic, incorporating [serpentine](/page/The_Serpentine) motifs drawn from the album's imagery.[[27]](#ref-27) Production manager Arthur Kemish handled logistics for the 53-show run, ensuring seamless execution across continents.[[28]](#ref-28)
Staging innovations centered on a dramatic V-shaped main stage spanning 55 meters wide, with each arm extending 33 meters to create a 66-meter performance area that immersed audiences in the narrative.[[28]](#ref-28) A 172-foot by 40-foot curved LED video wall dominated the backdrop, splitting into 12 movable columns that fragmented into 48 individual screens for dynamic projections of snakes and shadowy figures, enhancing the tour's cinematic feel.[[27]](#ref-27) The snake-like catwalk snaked through the crowd via two B-stages, allowing Swift to interact intimately, while a 30-foot inflatable cobra prop rose behind the stage during key moments, accompanied by thematic elements like a giant snake basket for dramatic entrances.[[28]](#ref-28) Confetti cannons and pyrotechnics punctuated high-energy sequences, with two flying gondolas enabling aerial movements that symbolized escape and empowerment.[[27]](#ref-27)
Rehearsals took place over four weeks at Rock Lititz in [Pennsylvania](/page/Pennsylvania), where the team constructed a partial setup due to venue height constraints, focusing on synchronizing the video mag deck—featuring shifting LED panels—with live [choreography](/page/Choreography) and lighting cues programmed by associate lighting designer Eric Marchwinski.[[28]](#ref-28) This process refined the tour's technical precision, including zip-line flights from front-of-house towers and the integration of a custom PA system hung on six 13-meter cantilevers for optimal sound distribution.[[26]](#ref-26)
Logistically, the production required four modular steel systems for the stage framework, each transported via 19 semi-trucks, totaling over 70 trucks alongside additional rigs for video, lighting, and [audio equipment](/page/Audio_equipment).[[28]](#ref-28) Safety protocols adhered to standard stadium-scale standards, including walk-through metal detectors for all attendees, venue-specific clear bag policies (e.g., A4 size in [Australia](/page/Australia), 12” x 6” x 12” in the [US](/page/United_States)), and prohibitions on professional cameras and large signs to mitigate risks in crowds exceeding 50,000.[[29]](#ref-29)[[30]](#ref-30) These measures, combined with on-site medical teams and evacuation plans, ensured secure operations throughout the international itinerary.[[30]](#ref-30)

## Set list and performances

### Standard set list

The standard [set list](/page/Set_list) for the Reputation Stadium Tour was structured to mirror the narrative arc of Taylor Swift's sixth studio album, [Reputation](/page/Reputation), progressing from themes of media scrutiny and defiance in the opening tracks to [vulnerability](/page/Vulnerability) and triumphant reclamation in the later sections, while incorporating select [hits](/page/Hits_+) from earlier albums to underscore her career evolution. This sequence emphasized 10 fixed tracks from [Reputation](/page/Reputation), with additional ones appearing in surprise segments, blending high-production numbers with intimate acoustic moments for dynamic pacing. The [set list](/page/Set_list) remained largely consistent across the 53-show run, with the fixed backbone providing a thematic journey from aggressive anthems to reflective ballads and celebratory closers.[[31]](#ref-31)
The full main set list, as performed on opening night in [Glendale, Arizona](/page/Glendale,_Arizona) (representative of the standard order, excluding one-off guest appearances), was as follows:

- "...Ready for It?"

- "[I Did Something Bad](/page/I_Did_Something_Bad)"

- "Gorgeous"

- "Style / Love Story / [You Belong with Me](/page/You_Belong_with_Me)" (medley)

- "[Look What You Made Me](/page/Look_What_You_Made_Me) Do"

- "End Game"

- "King of My Heart"

- "Delicate"

- "[Shake It Off](/page/Shake_It_Off)" (acoustic)

- "Dancing with Our Hands Tied" (acoustic)

- "[All Too Well](/page/All_Too_Well)" (acoustic)

- "[Blank Space](/page/Blank_Space)"

- "Dress"

- "Bad Blood / [Should've Said No](/page/Should)" (medley)

- "Don't Blame Me"

- "Long Live / [New Year's Day](/page/New_Year)" (medley, piano)

- "...Ready for It?" (reprise)

- "[Shake It Off](/page/Shake_It_Off)"

Subsequent shows featured variations in the acoustic segment (positions 9–11), where Swift performed a surprise song instead of fixed repeats like "Shake It Off," but the overall structure and remaining tracks stayed consistent to maintain the album's storytelling flow. The surprise song was a single acoustic performance on guitar or [piano](/page/Piano) during the b-stage, replacing the fixed acoustic tracks from opening night.[[2]](#ref-2)[[31]](#ref-31)
Performances were characterized by high-energy choreography involving 16 dancers in synchronized routines, particularly during Reputation-heavy segments like "[I Did Something Bad](/page/I_Did_Something_Bad)" and "Look What You Made Me Do," which incorporated snake-inspired visuals and [pyrotechnics](/page/Pyrotechnics) to evoke the album's motifs of rebirth and resilience. Swift underwent eight costume changes designed by [Jessica Jones](/page/Jessica_Jones), featuring glittering bodysuits, flowing gowns, and metallic ensembles in black, gold, and purple tones that aligned with the tour's dark, glamorous aesthetic—such as the sparkling black [jumpsuit](/page/Jumpsuit) for the opening act and the pink "cotton candy" [dress](/page/Dress) for acoustic interludes. Transitions between acts utilized massive LED screens displaying scrolling "news ticker" headlines mimicking tabloid gossip about Swift, reinforcing the [reputation](/page/Reputation) theme before seamlessly shifting to the next song via stage elevators and hydraulic platforms.[[32]](#ref-32)[[33]](#ref-33)[[34]](#ref-34)[[35]](#ref-35)
The set list evolved during pre-tour rehearsals in April 2018, where Swift and her team made final tweaks to song order and transitions for optimal pacing, ensuring the concert clocked in at approximately two hours while balancing high-production spectacle with emotional depth.[[36]](#ref-36)[[37]](#ref-37)

### Surprise songs and variations

The surprise songs segment of the Reputation Stadium Tour featured an acoustic encore where [Taylor Swift](/page/Taylor_Swift) performed one unique song per show, typically on [guitar](/page/Guitar) or [piano](/page/Piano) during the b-stage portion of the [concert](/page/Concert). This intimate interlude provided a stark contrast to the tour's high-production Reputation-focused setlist, emphasizing stripped-down renditions of rarities and deep cuts from her earlier discography to foster a personal connection with fans.[[5]](#ref-5)[[38]](#ref-38)
Across the tour's 53 dates from May to November 2018, Swift delivered 46 distinct surprise songs, with select tracks repeated at multiple venues to accommodate the schedule while maintaining variety.[[39]](#ref-39)[[40]](#ref-40) Notable examples included "All Too Well" from Red, performed in Glendale, Pasadena, and Arlington; "Wildest Dreams" from 1989 in Santa Clara; and "Holy Ground" from Red in Seattle.[[41]](#ref-41) Other rarities encompassed "Teardrops on My Guitar" from her debut album in East Rutherford and "The Best Day" from Fearless in Foxborough, highlighting her willingness to revisit pre-Reputation material.[[42]](#ref-42)
Selections often drew from fan favorites across eras like [1989](/page/1989), [Red](/page/Red), and [Speak Now](/page/Speak_Now), with variations such as mashups—including "Dancing with Our Hands Tied" blended with elements from other tracks in some performances—to add spontaneity and emotional depth.[[5]](#ref-5) This approach showcased the breadth of Swift's catalog, turning each show's acoustic moment into a highlight that rewarded dedicated attendees with exclusive live interpretations rarely heard in full-production settings.[[38]](#ref-38)

### Special guests

Throughout the Reputation Stadium Tour, Taylor Swift invited a variety of special guests to join her onstage for duets during the acoustic segment, creating collaborative highlights that amplified the tour's themes of camaraderie and defiance against public scrutiny. These appearances typically featured renditions of the guests' signature songs, selected for their energetic appeal and personal significance to Swift, and occurred on approximately 10 dates across the North American and European legs. The guests, often close friends or respected peers in pop and [country music](/page/Country_music), were chosen based on longstanding professional and personal connections, such as shared collaborations or mutual support during Swift's career challenges.[[43]](#ref-43)
Notable performances included Shawn Mendes dueting "There's Nothing Holdin' Me Back" at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California, on May 18, 2018, marking an early tour highlight with the Canadian singer's soaring vocals complementing Swift's.[[43]](#ref-43) The following night, May 19, 2018, at the same venue, Troye Sivan performed "My My My!" and Selena Gomez joined for "Hands to Myself," both longtime friends whose presence underscored themes of loyalty amid Swift's reputational battles.[[43]](#ref-43) In London at Wembley Stadium, Niall Horan sang "Slow Hands" on June 22, 2018, and Robbie Williams delivered "Angels" the next evening, June 23, infusing British flair into the international leg.[[43]](#ref-43) Other key moments featured Hayley Kiyoko on "Curious" at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, on July 26, 2018; Bryan Adams with "Summer of '69" at Rogers Stadium in Toronto on August 4, 2018; and Tim McGraw and Faith Hill revisiting Swift's debut single "Tim McGraw" at Nissan Stadium in Nashville on August 25, 2018, a nod to her country roots.[[44]](#ref-44)[[12]](#ref-12)
The tour's final U.S. shows on October 6, 2018, at [AT&T Stadium](/page/AT&T_Stadium) in [Arlington, Texas](/page/Arlington,_Texas), brought out multiple guests, including [Maren Morris](/page/Maren_Morris) for "The Middle" and [Sugarland](/page/Sugarland) for their co-written track "Babe," the latter making its live debut and emphasizing resilience through artistic partnerships.[[11]](#ref-11)[[45]](#ref-45) These collaborations, rehearsed discreetly to maintain surprise, extended set lists organically and heightened audience engagement by blending Swift's narrative-driven performance with guest artists' hits, often tying into Reputation's motifs of overcoming adversity through alliances.[[46]](#ref-46) In total, around 12 unique artists or groups appeared as special guests, fostering a sense of communal triumph that resonated with fans.[[44]](#ref-44)

## Tour itinerary

### North American leg

The North American leg of the Reputation Stadium Tour comprised 40 stadium concerts across 28 cities in the United States and [Canada](/page/Canada). The leg was split into two parts, spanning from May to early June 2018 and from late June to October 2018, with the European leg in between.[[39]](#ref-39) This portion marked Taylor Swift's first all-stadium outing, emphasizing large-scale production in major venues while navigating a packed schedule with brief interludes for international extensions.[[39]](#ref-39)

Regional highlights included sentimental homecoming performances, such as the August 25 concert at Nashville's Nissan Stadium, where Swift celebrated her [Tennessee](/page/Tennessee) origins by joining [Tim McGraw](/page/Tim_McGraw) and [Faith Hill](/page/Faith_Hill) onstage for a rendition of "Tim McGraw."[[12]](#ref-12) Similarly, the July 13–14 dates at Philadelphia's [Lincoln Financial Field](/page/Lincoln_Financial_Field) served as a personal return to her [Pennsylvania](/page/Pennsylvania) roots, with Swift visiting her childhood home in Reading beforehand.[[47]](#ref-47)
Logistically, Swift relied on private jet travel to cover the extensive North American distances efficiently between dates. Fan-organized meetups in host cities fostered pre-show excitement and community among attendees. Weather occasionally influenced performances, such as the rain-soaked shows at [MetLife Stadium](/page/MetLife_Stadium) on July 20–22, where Swift continued without major interruptions despite flash flood warnings.[[48]](#ref-48) The leg's second part concluded in Arlington on October 6, after which the tour proceeded to the [Oceania](/page/Oceania) leg.[[39]](#ref-39)

### European leg

The European leg of the Reputation Stadium Tour followed the initial North American shows, featuring six sold-out stadium shows across the [UK](/page/United_Kingdom) and [Ireland](/page/Ireland) in June 2018. These included two performances each at Etihad Stadium in [Manchester](/page/Manchester) on June 8 and 9, Croke Park in [Dublin](/page/Dublin) on June 15 and 16, and Wembley Stadium in [London](/page/London) on June 22 and 23. The leg drew a total attendance of approximately 353,000 fans, showcasing Swift's global appeal amid the album's themes of media scrutiny and personal reinvention.[[39]](#ref-39)
To suit European audiences, the tour incorporated adjustments such as earlier evening start times—Taylor [Swift](/page/Taylor_Swift) took the stage at 8:15 p.m. at [Wembley](/page/Wembley), aligning with local preferences compared to later North American slots around 8:45 p.m. or later—while maintaining the core staging and setlist integrity. International fan travel was encouraged through bundled ticket and accommodation packages offered via official partners like [Ticketmaster](/page/Ticketmaster), facilitating attendance from across Europe and beyond. Local promotion was amplified by [BBC](/page/BBC) coverage, including news features on the Manchester opener where [Swift](/page/Taylor_Swift) acknowledged the city's resilience post-2017 bombing, and interviews highlighting the tour's cultural impact.[[49]](#ref-49)[[50]](#ref-50)[[51]](#ref-51)
The Wembley shows stood out as the leg's high-profile finale, with back-to-back sell-outs attracting 143,427 attendees and generating over $12 million in revenue. Special guests enhanced the excitement, including [Robbie Williams](/page/Robbie_Williams) joining Swift for renditions of his 1997 hit "Angels" on both nights, a nod to British pop heritage. [Niall Horan](/page/Niall_Horan) performed "Slow Hands" at the London Wembley show on June 22, adding to the collaborative energy. European fans responded enthusiastically to the production's "American" motifs—like snake imagery symbolizing media attacks and references to U.S. [celebrity culture](/page/Celebrity_culture)—interpreting them through a universal lens of personal empowerment, resulting in loud sing-alongs and visible emotional connections during songs like "Look What You Made Me Do."[[39]](#ref-39)[[52]](#ref-52)[[53]](#ref-53)
The leg wrapped with the June 23 Wembley performance, serving as a triumphant close to the European extension before the tour resumed in [North America](/page/North_America). Swift later reflected on this phase in the Netflix concert film reputation Stadium Tour, noting how the overseas crowds' passion helped her reclaim her narrative after years of public challenges, affirming the tour's role in fostering deeper fan bonds worldwide.[[54]](#ref-54)

### Oceania leg

The Oceania leg of the Reputation Stadium Tour featured five sold-out stadium shows in [Australia](/page/Australia) and [New Zealand](/page/New_Zealand) in October and November 2018, supported by [Charli XCX](/page/Charli_XCX) and [Broods](/page/Broods). This leg highlighted Swift's expansion to the region, with performances in major venues drawing enthusiastic crowds.[[8]](#ref-8)

### Japanese leg

The Japanese leg consisted of two sold-out shows at [Tokyo Dome](/page/Tokyo_Dome) in [Tokyo](/page/Tokyo), [Japan](/page/Japan), on November 20 and 21, 2018, supported by [Charli XCX](/page/Charli_XCX). The performances drew 100,109 attendees, generating significant revenue and closing the tour on a high note with pyrotechnics and full production.[[7]](#ref-7)

## Commercial performance

### Ticket sales and attendance

The ticket sales for Taylor Swift's Reputation Stadium Tour were managed through a presale system via the Taylor Swift Tix portal, where fans registered and earned "boosts" to improve their access priority by purchasing the reputation album, merchandise, or referring friends.[[23]](#ref-23)[[55]](#ref-55) This incentive structure aimed to prioritize dedicated fans, with presale windows running from December 5 to 8, 2017, ahead of the general public onsale on December 13.[[23]](#ref-23)
The general onsale on [Ticketmaster](/page/Ticketmaster) drew significant fan frustration due to high face-value prices ranging from $50 to over $350, the immediate appearance of resale listings despite the Verified Fan system, and the introduction of "Official Platinum" premium seats not available during presale.[[56]](#ref-56)[[57]](#ref-57) While initial sales varied by market—with some shows lingering with available seats—demand ultimately led to all 53 dates selling out, reflecting the tour's strong popularity. [Secondary market](/page/Secondary_market) prices indicated robust aftermarket interest.[[58]](#ref-58)
The tour attracted a total attendance of 2.9 million across its 53 stadium shows, establishing it as one of the decade's major draws.[[59]](#ref-59) Notable peaks included over 118,000 attendees across two nights at the Rose Bowl in [Pasadena, California](/page/Pasadena,_California), and 107,550 at [Levi's Stadium](/page/Levi) in Santa Clara over two performances, both setting venue records for the artist.[[60]](#ref-60)

### Gross revenue and boxscore

The Reputation Stadium Tour generated a total gross revenue of $345.7 million from 53 shows across [North America](/page/North_America), [Europe](/page/Europe), [Oceania](/page/Oceania), and [Asia](/page/Asia), establishing it as the highest-grossing tour by a female artist in history at the time of its completion.[[7]](#ref-7) This financial success reflected strong global demand, with an average per-show gross of approximately $6.5 million.[[7]](#ref-7) In the United States alone, the tour earned $266.1 million from 38 shows and 2,068,399 tickets sold, surpassing the previous record for the highest-grossing U.S. tour held by [the Rolling Stones](/page/The_Rolling_Stones)' [A Bigger Bang Tour](/page/A_Bigger_Bang_Tour) ($245 million from 2005–2007).[[8]](#ref-8)
Key boxscore highlights underscored the tour's economic impact. The Reputation Stadium Tour was the fifth headlining [concert tour](/page/Concert_tour) by American [singer-songwriter](/page/Singer-songwriter) [Taylor Swift](/page/Taylor_Swift), and her first to exclusively play stadium venues, launched to promote her sixth studio album, [Reputation](/page/Reputation) (2017).[[1]](#ref-1)[[2]](#ref-2)
The tour consisted of 53 shows across seven countries—[United States](/page/United_States), [Canada](/page/Canada), [United Kingdom](/page/United_Kingdom), [Ireland](/page/Ireland), [Australia](/page/Australia), [New Zealand](/page/New_Zealand), and [Japan](/page/Japan)—beginning on May 8, 2018, at [University of Phoenix](/page/University_of_Phoenix) Stadium in [Glendale, Arizona](/page/Glendale,_Arizona), and ending on November 21, 2018, at [Tokyo Dome](/page/Tokyo_Dome) in [Tokyo](/page/Tokyo), [Japan](/page/Japan).[[3]](#ref-3)[[4]](#ref-4) Featuring elaborate production elements including a snake-inspired stage design, massive LED screens, hydraulic platforms, and fireworks, the shows typically lasted nearly two hours and included a mix of [Reputation](/page/Reputation) tracks alongside hits from Swift's earlier albums, with nightly acoustic "surprise songs" performed on secondary stages.[[1]](#ref-1)[[2]](#ref-2)[[5]](#ref-5)
Opening acts varied by leg, with [Camila Cabello](/page/Camila_Cabello) and [Charli XCX](/page/Charli_XCX) supporting the North American and European dates, while [Broods](/page/Broods) joined for the [Oceania](/page/Oceania) shows.[[6]](#ref-6) The tour was a commercial juggernaut, grossing $345.7 million from 2.9 million tickets sold, marking it as the highest-grossing U.S. tour in boxscore history at the time and Swift's biggest earner until her [Eras Tour](/page/The_Eras_Tour).[[7]](#ref-7)[[8]](#ref-8)[[9]](#ref-9)
Critics praised the tour for its high-energy spectacle, Swift's vocal prowess, and thematic cohesion tying into Reputation's narrative of resilience and reinvention, with reviews hailing it as the peak of her live performances and one of the best tours of 2018.[[10]](#ref-10)[[1]](#ref-1) Notable moments included surprise guest appearances by artists like [Maren Morris](/page/Maren_Morris), [Tim McGraw](/page/Tim_McGraw), and [Faith Hill](/page/Faith_Hill), as well as Swift's philanthropic efforts, including inviting 2,000 foster and adopted children to a pre-tour rehearsal concert in [Arizona](/page/Arizona) for free.[[11]](#ref-11)[[12]](#ref-12)[[13]](#ref-13)
The tour's Dallas show on October 6, 2018, was documented in the Netflix concert film Taylor Swift: Reputation Stadium Tour, directed by Paul Dugdale, which premiered on December 31, 2018, and highlighted behind-the-scenes preparations alongside full performances, earning acclaim for its intimate portrayal of Swift's artistry amid intense media scrutiny. The film was later made available for purchase and rental on various platforms after leaving Netflix in 2023.[[14]](#ref-14)[[15]](#ref-15)[[16]](#ref-16)

## Background and development

### Announcement and promotion

Taylor Swift announced the Reputation Stadium Tour on November 13, 2017, via her official website and social media channels, shortly after the release of her sixth studio album, Reputation, on November 10, 2017.[[17]](#ref-17) The initial reveal detailed the first leg of 27 stadium shows across North America, set to commence on May 8, 2018, at University of Phoenix Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, and conclude on October 6, 2018, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.[[18]](#ref-18) This tour marked Swift's first all-stadium production and was explicitly positioned in support of Reputation, an album exploring themes of intense media scrutiny on her personal life and personal empowerment amid public backlash.[[19]](#ref-19)
Promotional efforts for the tour were deeply integrated with the album's marketing campaign, which had begun earlier in 2017 with a deliberate [social media](/page/Social_media) blackout across Swift's platforms in late August, followed by cryptic teasers such as timestamped videos and newspaper-style advertisements hinting at reclaiming her [narrative](/page/Narrative).[[20]](#ref-20) Key singles like "...Ready for It?", released as a promotional track on September 3, 2017, and sent to radio on October 24, 2017, built anticipation by showcasing the album's bold, trap-influenced sound that aligned with the tour's high-energy [stadium](/page/Stadium) format.[[21]](#ref-21) Exclusive merchandise lines, including apparel and accessories themed around Reputation's snake motif and dark aesthetic, were launched alongside the [album](/page/Album) and extended into tour-specific items available through presales, further immersing fans in the album's [narrative](/page/Narrative) of resilience.[[22]](#ref-22)
To facilitate fan access, Swift implemented the Taylor Swift Tix program, a verified fan system where participants earned "boosts" toward presale eligibility by engaging with her [music](/page/Music), such as purchasing [Reputation](/page/Reputation) or streaming videos, rewarding dedicated supporters with priority entry starting December 5, 2017.[[23]](#ref-23) General ticket sales opened on December 13, 2017, via [Ticketmaster](/page/Ticketmaster), with subsequent announcements adding European dates in December 2017, [Oceania](/page/Oceania) leg in May 2018, and Japan dates in August 2018, the tour ultimately expanding to 53 shows across [North America](/page/North_America), [Europe](/page/Europe), [Oceania](/page/Oceania), and [Asia](/page/Asia) to meet demand, emphasizing Swift's strategy of direct fan engagement over traditional media promotion.[[24]](#ref-24)[[25]](#ref-25)

### Production and staging

The production of Taylor Swift's Reputation Stadium Tour was led by show director and lighting designer Baz Halpin, who oversaw the integration of theatrical elements with high-tech visuals to embody the album's themes of media scrutiny and rebirth.[[26]](#ref-26) Associate director Melissa Garcia collaborated closely with Halpin to choreograph transitions between performance segments, while [production designer](/page/Production_designer) Tamlyn Wright crafted the overall aesthetic, incorporating [serpentine](/page/The_Serpentine) motifs drawn from the album's imagery.[[27]](#ref-27) Production manager Arthur Kemish handled logistics for the 53-show run, ensuring seamless execution across continents.[[28]](#ref-28)
Staging innovations centered on a dramatic V-shaped main stage spanning 55 meters wide, with each arm extending 33 meters to create a 66-meter performance area that immersed audiences in the narrative.[[28]](#ref-28) A 172-foot by 40-foot curved LED video wall dominated the backdrop, splitting into 12 movable columns that fragmented into 48 individual screens for dynamic projections of snakes and shadowy figures, enhancing the tour's cinematic feel.[[27]](#ref-27) The snake-like catwalk snaked through the crowd via two B-stages, allowing Swift to interact intimately, while a 30-foot inflatable cobra prop rose behind the stage during key moments, accompanied by thematic elements like a giant snake basket for dramatic entrances.[[28]](#ref-28) Confetti cannons and pyrotechnics punctuated high-energy sequences, with two flying gondolas enabling aerial movements that symbolized escape and empowerment.[[27]](#ref-27)
Rehearsals took place over four weeks at Rock Lititz in [Pennsylvania](/page/Pennsylvania), where the team constructed a partial setup due to venue height constraints, focusing on synchronizing the video mag deck—featuring shifting LED panels—with live [choreography](/page/Choreography) and lighting cues programmed by associate lighting designer Eric Marchwinski.[[28]](#ref-28) This process refined the tour's technical precision, including zip-line flights from front-of-house towers and the integration of a custom PA system hung on six 13-meter cantilevers for optimal sound distribution.[[26]](#ref-26)
Logistically, the production required four modular steel systems for the stage framework, each transported via 19 semi-trucks, totaling over 70 trucks alongside additional rigs for video, lighting, and [audio equipment](/page/Audio_equipment).[[28]](#ref-28) Safety protocols adhered to standard stadium-scale standards, including walk-through metal detectors for all attendees, venue-specific clear bag policies (e.g., A4 size in [Australia](/page/Australia), 12” x 6” x 12” in the [US](/page/United_States)), and prohibitions on professional cameras and large signs to mitigate risks in crowds exceeding 50,000.[[29]](#ref-29)[[30]](#ref-30) These measures, combined with on-site medical teams and evacuation plans, ensured secure operations throughout the international itinerary.[[30]](#ref-30)

## Set list and performances

### Standard set list

The standard [set list](/page/Set_list) for the Reputation Stadium Tour was structured to mirror the narrative arc of Taylor Swift's sixth studio album, [Reputation](/page/Reputation), progressing from themes of media scrutiny and defiance in the opening tracks to [vulnerability](/page/Vulnerability) and triumphant reclamation in the later sections, while incorporating select [hits](/page/Hits_+) from earlier albums to underscore her career evolution. This sequence emphasized 10 fixed tracks from [Reputation](/page/Reputation), with additional ones appearing in surprise segments, blending high-production numbers with intimate acoustic moments for dynamic pacing. The [set list](/page/Set_list) remained largely consistent across the 53-show run, with the fixed backbone providing a thematic journey from aggressive anthems to reflective ballads and celebratory closers.[[31]](#ref-31)
The full main set list, as performed on opening night in [Glendale, Arizona](/page/Glendale,_Arizona) (representative of the standard order, excluding one-off guest appearances), was as follows:

- "...Ready for It?"

- "[I Did Something Bad](/page/I_Did_Something_Bad)"

- "Gorgeous"

- "Style / Love Story / [You Belong with Me](/page/You_Belong_with_Me)" (medley)

- "[Look What You Made Me](/page/Look_What_You_Made_Me) Do"

- "End Game"

- "King of My Heart"

- "Delicate"

- "[Shake It Off](/page/Shake_It_Off)" (acoustic)

- "Dancing with Our Hands Tied" (acoustic)

- "[All Too Well](/page/All_Too_Well)" (acoustic)

- "[Blank Space](/page/Blank_Space)"

- "Dress"

- "Bad Blood / [Should've Said No](/page/Should)" (medley)

- "Don't Blame Me"

- "Long Live / [New Year's Day](/page/New_Year)" (medley, piano)

- "...Ready for It?" (reprise)

- "[Shake It Off](/page/Shake_It_Off)"

Subsequent shows featured variations in the acoustic segment (positions 9–11), where Swift performed a surprise song instead of fixed repeats like "Shake It Off," but the overall structure and remaining tracks stayed consistent to maintain the album's storytelling flow. The surprise song was a single acoustic performance on guitar or [piano](/page/Piano) during the b-stage, replacing the fixed acoustic tracks from opening night.[[2]](#ref-2)[[31]](#ref-31)
Performances were characterized by high-energy choreography involving 16 dancers in synchronized routines, particularly during Reputation-heavy segments like "[I Did Something Bad](/page/I_Did_Something_Bad)" and "Look What You Made Me Do," which incorporated snake-inspired visuals and [pyrotechnics](/page/Pyrotechnics) to evoke the album's motifs of rebirth and resilience. Swift underwent eight costume changes designed by [Jessica Jones](/page/Jessica_Jones), featuring glittering bodysuits, flowing gowns, and metallic ensembles in black, gold, and purple tones that aligned with the tour's dark, glamorous aesthetic—such as the sparkling black [jumpsuit](/page/Jumpsuit) for the opening act and the pink "cotton candy" [dress](/page/Dress) for acoustic interludes. Transitions between acts utilized massive LED screens displaying scrolling "news ticker" headlines mimicking tabloid gossip about Swift, reinforcing the [reputation](/page/Reputation) theme before seamlessly shifting to the next song via stage elevators and hydraulic platforms.[[32]](#ref-32)[[33]](#ref-33)[[34]](#ref-34)[[35]](#ref-35)
The set list evolved during pre-tour rehearsals in April 2018, where Swift and her team made final tweaks to song order and transitions for optimal pacing, ensuring the concert clocked in at approximately two hours while balancing high-production spectacle with emotional depth.[[36]](#ref-36)[[37]](#ref-37)

### Surprise songs and variations

The surprise songs segment of the Reputation Stadium Tour featured an acoustic encore where [Taylor Swift](/page/Taylor_Swift) performed one unique song per show, typically on [guitar](/page/Guitar) or [piano](/page/Piano) during the b-stage portion of the [concert](/page/Concert). This intimate interlude provided a stark contrast to the tour's high-production Reputation-focused setlist, emphasizing stripped-down renditions of rarities and deep cuts from her earlier discography to foster a personal connection with fans.[[5]](#ref-5)[[38]](#ref-38)
Across the tour's 53 dates from May to November 2018, Swift delivered 46 distinct surprise songs, with select tracks repeated at multiple venues to accommodate the schedule while maintaining variety.[[39]](#ref-39)[[40]](#ref-40) Notable examples included "All Too Well" from Red, performed in Glendale, Pasadena, and Arlington; "Wildest Dreams" from 1989 in Santa Clara; and "Holy Ground" from Red in Seattle.[[41]](#ref-41) Other rarities encompassed "Teardrops on My Guitar" from her debut album in East Rutherford and "The Best Day" from Fearless in Foxborough, highlighting her willingness to revisit pre-Reputation material.[[42]](#ref-42)
Selections often drew from fan favorites across eras like [1989](/page/1989), [Red](/page/Red), and [Speak Now](/page/Speak_Now), with variations such as mashups—including "Dancing with Our Hands Tied" blended with elements from other tracks in some performances—to add spontaneity and emotional depth.[[5]](#ref-5) This approach showcased the breadth of Swift's catalog, turning each show's acoustic moment into a highlight that rewarded dedicated attendees with exclusive live interpretations rarely heard in full-production settings.[[38]](#ref-38)

### Special guests

Throughout the Reputation Stadium Tour, Taylor Swift invited a variety of special guests to join her onstage for duets during the acoustic segment, creating collaborative highlights that amplified the tour's themes of camaraderie and defiance against public scrutiny. These appearances typically featured renditions of the guests' signature songs, selected for their energetic appeal and personal significance to Swift, and occurred on approximately 10 dates across the North American and European legs. The guests, often close friends or respected peers in pop and [country music](/page/Country_music), were chosen based on longstanding professional and personal connections, such as shared collaborations or mutual support during Swift's career challenges.[[43]](#ref-43)
Notable performances included Shawn Mendes dueting "There's Nothing Holdin' Me Back" at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California, on May 18, 2018, marking an early tour highlight with the Canadian singer's soaring vocals complementing Swift's.[[43]](#ref-43) The following night, May 19, 2018, at the same venue, Troye Sivan performed "My My My!" and Selena Gomez joined for "Hands to Myself," both longtime friends whose presence underscored themes of loyalty amid Swift's reputational battles.[[43]](#ref-43) In London at Wembley Stadium, Niall Horan sang "Slow Hands" on June 22, 2018, and Robbie Williams delivered "Angels" the next evening, June 23, infusing British flair into the international leg.[[43]](#ref-43) Other key moments featured Hayley Kiyoko on "Curious" at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, on July 26, 2018; Bryan Adams with "Summer of '69" at Rogers Stadium in Toronto on August 4, 2018; and Tim McGraw and Faith Hill revisiting Swift's debut single "Tim McGraw" at Nissan Stadium in Nashville on August 25, 2018, a nod to her country roots.[[44]](#ref-44)[[12]](#ref-12)
The tour's final U.S. shows on October 6, 2018, at [AT&T Stadium](/page/AT&T_Stadium) in [Arlington, Texas](/page/Arlington,_Texas), brought out multiple guests, including [Maren Morris](/page/Maren_Morris) for "The Middle" and [Sugarland](/page/Sugarland) for their co-written track "Babe," the latter making its live debut and emphasizing resilience through artistic partnerships.[[11]](#ref-11)[[45]](#ref-45) These collaborations, rehearsed discreetly to maintain surprise, extended set lists organically and heightened audience engagement by blending Swift's narrative-driven performance with guest artists' hits, often tying into Reputation's motifs of overcoming adversity through alliances.[[46]](#ref-46) In total, around 12 unique artists or groups appeared as special guests, fostering a sense of communal triumph that resonated with fans.[[44]](#ref-44)

## Tour itinerary

### North American leg
